fit: olive-oil diet score in spondyloarthritis and bone density
assessment: P629 reports a higher oil score in normal bone density. The oil grade and Parkinson constipation response are unmeasured. P628 may share participants.

fit: dietary caffeine intake in Parkinson and pooled caffeine in spinocerebellar ataxia
assessment: Two distinct abstracts link this exposure to separate dietary contexts. Neither estimates brewed coffee and clinical fatigue.

fit: corn-oil comparison group in a mouse toxicology experiment
assessment: The five-arm study includes corn oil but reports endocrine and histology outcomes. Refined grade and Parkinson rest tremor are unverified.

fit: patient-reported turmeric and pain in axial spondyloarthritis
assessment: The English and French reports describe the same 39-person survey. A reported easing impression lacks a turmeric-specific count, preparation, comparator or Parkinson outcome.

fit: trustworthiness-screened pooled extract and pain outcomes in knee osteoarthritis
assessment: Four separate placebo comparisons pooled to 0.72 points less pain on a 0–10 scale, low certainty and below 1.5 points. The extract evidence does not measure culinary turmeric or Parkinson pain.

fit: proprietary water-dispersible turmeric extract in knee osteoarthritis
assessment: Mean reductions 14.41 versus 6.02 mm on a 100-mm VAS in 139 analyzed adults. Formulation and population differ. Inclusion in the published pooled review remains unresolved.

fit: aggregate clinical outcomes from a Parkinson nanomicelle curcumin trial
assessment: Randomized 60 people to formulated curcumin or placebo. The reported aggregate results give no pain or discomfort item direction and do not test culinary ground turmeric.
